title: E. Supersequence
statement:
An array $$a$$ is called a subsequence of an array $$b$$ if some elements can be removed from array $$b$$ (possibly all, possibly none) to obtain the array $$a$$.

You are given an array $$a = [a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n]$$. We call an array $$b = [b_1, b_2, \dots, b_m]$$ beautiful if:

You have to process $$q$$ queries. In the $$i$$-th query, a single integer $$x_i$$ is given. Your task is as follows:

The first line contains two integers $$n$$ and $$q$$ ($$1 $\leq n, q \leq 2 \cdot 10^5$$$).

The second line contains $$n$$ integers $$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$$ ($$1 $\leq a_i \leq 10^9$$$).

The third line contains $$q$$ integers $$x_1, x_2, \dots, x_q$$ ($$1 $\leq x_i \leq 10^{18}$$$).

For each query, print a single integer — the answer to it.
input: Input The first line contains two integers $$n$$ and $$q$$ ($$1 $\leq n, q \leq 2 \cdot 10^5$$$). The second line contains $$n$$ integers $$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$$ ($$1 $\leq a_i \leq 10^9$$$). The third line contains $$q$$ integers $$x_1, x_2, \dots, x_q$$ ($$1 $\leq x_i \leq 10^{18}$$$).
output: Output For each query, print a single integer — the answer to it.
